speculative_loading_surface_label: Example speculative-loading posture for official voter-information routes
delivery_role_note: The service reviews which public routes may be prefetched or prerendered before view and which must never be speculated because fetch/render itself could create side effects or stale-answer risk.

reviewed_target_classes.class_note: Low-variance informational pages may be eligible for prefetch when reviewed as side-effect free.
Refresh-safe confirmation pages may be considered for speculation only if activation cannot outrun real acceptance state.
Routes whose GET or load behavior can send codes, change session state, or consume one-time actions are excluded from speculation.

allowed_prerender_routes.activation_guard_note: Client-side effects remain deferred until actual activation.

excluded_route_classes.exclusion_note: A speculative GET or hidden prerender must not send codes, consume tokens, or advance the public workflow.
Rapidly changing pages are excluded unless stale-speculation eviction is explicitly reviewed.

activation_boundary_note: Prerendered routes do not treat background load as user arrival and defer viewed-state side effects until activation.
server_side_effect_guard_note: Speculative requests are reviewed so GET alone does not mutate server-visible state that should wait for explicit user action.
client_side_effect_guard_note: Background prerender code defers analytics, storage mutation, timers, and similar user-arrival side effects until actual activation.
varying_state_freshness_note: Reviewed routes distinguish stable content from targets whose answer may drift between speculation time and activation time.
stale_speculation_eviction_note: The service keeps a bounded way to discard stale prefetched or prerendered state when the governing public answer changes.
support_variance_note: Speculative loading is treated as optional acceleration rather than as a correctness requirement across all browsers.
